commands.review_summary:
The branch converts canonical safe-integer cron delivery thread IDs back to numbers when reading SQLite delivery columns and adds cron store regression tests.

PR surface: Source +5, Tests +34. Total +39 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection: current main stores delivery.threadId in a TEXT column with String(...) and deliveryFromRow returns that TEXT value directly, so numeric inputs lose their numeric type after a SQLite round trip. I did not run tests because this review was read-only.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] There is a concrete, narrow repair path: preserve string-vs-number threadId identity on the cron SQLite load path instead of guessing from the TEXT column alone.

target.title: fix(cron): preserve numeric delivery thread id across SQLite round-trip
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cron job's delivery target can carry a `threadId` that is legitimately either a string or a number (`string | number`). The input schema (`src/cron/delivery-field-schemas.ts`) accepts `z.union([TrimmedNonEmptyStringFieldSchema, z.number().finite()])` and `normalizeCronJobInput` deliberately preserves a numeric thread id. Numeric thread ids are real: for example a Telegram forum/topic id like `1008013`.

The SQLite codec collapses that type. On write it stores the thread id as TEXT via `String(...)`, and on read it hands the raw TEXT column straight back:

```ts
// src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts write path
delivery_thread_id:
  delivery?.threadId === undefined || delivery.threadId === null
    ? null
    : String(delivery.threadId),

// src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts read path (before)
...(row.delivery_thread_id ? { threadId: row.delivery_thread_id } : {}),
```

So a persistence round-trip silently changes the type:

```
INPUT  threadId: 1008013   (number)
LOADED threadId: "1008013" (string)
```

This matters because the reloaded value is what the live delivery path consumes. `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` runs it through `normalizeOptionalThreadValue`, which keeps the string-vs-number distinction rather than re-normalizing it. A freshly created in-memory job carries `threadId: 1008013` (number); the same job after a save/reload carries `"1008013"` (string). Identical config produces two different runtime types depending on whether the job came from disk or memory. Some channel adapters re-coerce (Telegram's `parseTelegramThreadId` accepts both), but others require a number: the Telegram native approval path only sets `messageThreadId` when `typeof threadId === "number"` (`extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.ts`), so a reloaded string-typed topic id is dropped there.

## Why This Change Was Made

The column is TEXT, so both `1008013` and `"1008013"` are already stored as the same bytes; the fix belongs on the read boundary that reconstructs the runtime value. `deliveryFromRow` is the single persistence read surface (the config sidecar in `row-codec.ts` is projected from it), so fixing it there aligns both the store and sidecar copies of a job.

```ts
// src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts (after)
function threadIdFromColumn(value: string): string | number {
  const numeric = Number(value);
  return Number.isSafeInteger(numeric) && String(numeric) === value ? numeric : value;
}
// ...
...(row.delivery_thread_id ? { threadId: threadIdFromColumn(row.delivery_thread_id) } : {}),
```

A stored value is reconstructed as a number only when it is the canonical decimal form of a safe integer (`String(Number(value)) === value`). This matches the truncated-integer contract of `normalizeOptionalThreadValue` and is lossless for every non-canonical string: `"007"`, `"1e3"`, `"12.5"`, `"topic-9"`, and any non-numeric id stay strings and round-trip unchanged. The write path stays `String(...)`, which is correct for a TEXT column. No schema change or migration is needed, and existing persisted rows benefit immediately.

## User Impact

Cron jobs configured with a numeric delivery thread id (for example a Telegram forum/topic id) now deliver to the same thread whether the job is served from memory or reloaded from SQLite. Previously a save/reload silently retyped the id to a string, which downstream paths that require a numeric thread id (such as Telegram native approval delivery) would drop, sending to the general chat instead of the topic.

## Evidence

Verification:
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts src/cron/store.test.ts` -> clean.
- `oxfmt --check src/cron/store/delivery-codec.ts src/cron/store.test.ts` -> clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json` -> no errors.
- Added colocated regression tests in `src/cron/store.test.ts` (numeric thread id reloads as a number; non-numeric `"007"` stays a string). vitest could not be run in this checkout (worker startup is killed by the sandbox resource governor); the same save/load assertions are demonstrated live below and the tests run in CI.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a numeric cron delivery thread id (e.g. Telegram topic id 1008013) is retyped to a string by a SQLite save/reload, diverging from the same job held in memory.
Real environment tested: drove the real `saveCronStore`/`loadCronStore` from `src/cron/store.ts` and the real `resolveCronDeliveryPlan` from `src/cron/delivery-plan.ts` against a real temp SQLite state DB (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`), on pristine main and on the patched tree. Nothing was stubbed: the real codec, the real Kysely store, and the real delivery-plan resolver all ran; only the state directory was a throwaway temp dir.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: create a job with `delivery.threadId: 1008013` (number) and a second job with `delivery.threadId: "007"` (string), `saveCronStore`, then `loadCronStore`, and inspect the reloaded delivery thread id plus `resolveCronDeliveryPlan(job).threadId`.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main delivery-codec.ts)
numeric input  threadId: 1008013 (number)
numeric loaded threadId: "1008013" string
numeric plan   threadId: "1008013" string
numeric matches in-memory job: false
string  input  threadId: "007" (string)
string  loaded threadId: "007" string
# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
numeric input  threadId: 1008013 (number)
numeric loaded threadId: 1008013 number
numeric plan   threadId: 1008013 number
numeric matches in-memory job: true
string  input  threadId: "007" (string)
string  loaded threadId: "007" string
```
Observed result after fix: the reloaded numeric thread id and the resolved delivery-plan thread id come back as the number 1008013 and match the in-memory job, while the non-numeric "007" id stays a string, so the persistence round-trip no longer changes the value's type.
What was not tested: no live Telegram send (the downstream drop is shown by reading `approval-handler.runtime.ts`, not by a live topic post); vitest and full build were not run in this checkout.
